reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Ps 119 is an identity-numbering psalm (web:Ps.119.1 maps to oshb:Ps.119.1 and web:Ps.119.176 to oshb:Ps.119.176 in the offset map; verse_map_web.json holds 176 keys for Ps 119 and 0 of them is a Ps.119.0 title pseudo-ref, this psalm having no superscription), so the row's web:/oshb: pairing is arithmetically correct and citation_sweep.py returns GREEN on it. Collated both Hebrew runs from the source bytes: אַשְׁרֵ֥י (oshb:Ps.119.1) and בַּמֶּ֣ה (oshb:Ps.119.9) both return tier byte, and both are the whole verse-initial token of their verse (quote length equals first-token length; the following character is a space), so the quote is neither truncated nor re-cut. I rebuilt the acrostic from consonantal_index.json rather than trusting the row or the device inventory: the first skeleton character of each of the 8 verses Ps.119.1-Ps.119.8 is one and the same letter, and the same test run over all 22 stanzas of the psalm is uniform in 22 of 22 - so the tier-1 warrant holds and the seam contrast at Ps.119.8|Ps.119.9 is real. The doubled-beatitude claim is byte-supported: skeleton sweep of the 'ashre spelling returns 2 verses inside this span, Ps.119.1 and Ps.119.2, and 0 verses in the other seven stanzas of this cluster; the pointed openers are אַשְׁרֵ֥י (oshb:Ps.119.1) and אַ֭שְׁרֵי (oshb:Ps.119.2), both byte tier. WEB is verbatim at both refs (check_web_quotes.py passes them). No selah, no paseq, no ketiv/qere and no reversed-nun or suspended-letter entry falls in Ps.119.1-Ps.119.8 in pmarks_Ps.json, so there is no disclosure gap to close; the row makes no mark claim. Observation only: the stanza_header value is WEB typography (tier-4) and the row lists it among observed_substrate_signals, but it is explicitly distinguished there from a superscription and the rationale's warrant rests on the skeleton bytes, so nothing tier-4 is load-bearing. Confidence high is calibrated for a stanza whose letter test is exceptionless in 8 of 8 verses.

The substance of this row verifies. בַּמֶּ֣ה (oshb:Ps.119.9) and גְּמֹ֖ל (oshb:Ps.119.17) both collate at byte tier and are whole verse-initial tokens. The BETH letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.9-Ps.119.16 in the skeleton, and Ps.119.17 heads a different letter, so the seam at Ps.119.16|Ps.119.17 is tier-1 warranted. Numbering is identity, dual-citation arithmetic is correct, check_refs_mirror.py returns 0 flags (Ps.119.12 and Ps.119.17 are both mirrored), and pmarks_Ps.json puts no selah, paseq or ketiv/qere entry anywhere in Ps.119.9-Ps.119.16, so no disclosure is owed. Calling Ps.119.12 the middle of the run is loose - it is the 4th of the 8 verses - but not wrong enough to contest. The defect is one layer down: the device_notes field repeats the WEB quotation without any web: ref beside it, which the campaign's quote-anchoring rule makes mandatory at every layer, and which is exactly what check_web_quotes.py flags.

challenges.claim: The curly-quoted WEB span in M8-Ps-402's device_notes carries no web: ref in the same field, violating the mandatory in-field anchoring of WEB quotations at every layer.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py over this row alone reports flag_count 1 of 11 quotes checked, at path [1].device_notes, with issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field'; refs_nearby is the empty list. The span itself is fidelity-clean - it is verbatim WEB at web:Ps.119.12, “Blessed are you, Yahweh. Teach me your statutes.” (web:Ps.119.12), and the identical span in the rationale field passes because the ref sits beside it there. So this is an anchoring defect, not a gloss-as-WEB defect, and the repair is the insertion of the one ref token web:Ps.119.12 into device_notes. The other 10 curly spans across this cluster's 8 rows all pass, which is why the omission reads as a slip rather than a house style.

reviews.reasoning: Verified independently. גְּמֹ֖ל (oshb:Ps.119.17) and דָּֽבְקָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.119.25) both collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens, and the GIMEL letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.17-Ps.119.24 in the skeleton, with a different letter at Ps.119.25 - a clean tier-1 seam at Ps.119.24|Ps.119.25. The cross-stanza motif claim is the part worth testing, and it survives: a skeleton sweep of the sarim spelling returns exactly 2 verses in the whole of Ps 119, Ps.119.23 (שרים) and Ps.119.161 (שרים), and Ps.119.161 is indeed the opening verse of the psalm's 21st stanza, whose WEB stanza_header reads SIN AND SHIN. Both are mirrored correctly - web:Ps.119.161 sits in boundary_evidence_refs, and check_refs_mirror.py returns 0 flags - and the row explicitly denies the motif any boundary force, which is the right handling for a device that would otherwise argue continuity across two stanza seams. Ps.119.161 is one of the 3 ketiv/qere verses of Ps 119 in pmarks_Ps.json (with Ps.119.79 and Ps.119.147) and its skeleton carries the inline-ketiv doubling, but the row cites the verse without quoting its Hebrew and its argument rests on the sarim token, which is not the ketiv/qere word, so no K/Q disclosure is owed. Observation, not a challenge: describing the stanza as closing under princes' scorn is imprecise, since the sarim verse is Ps.119.23 while the closing verse reads “Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors.” (web:Ps.119.24); the characterization is loose but the boundary warrant does not lean on it.

The boundary itself is sound and I do not contest the span. דָּֽבְקָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.119.25) and הוֹרֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.119.33) collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens, the DALETH letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.25-Ps.119.32, and Ps.119.33 heads a different letter. The device note about the stanza's own inclusio is byte-true: a skeleton sweep of the dbq spelling returns exactly 2 verses in the whole of Ps 119, and both fall inside this span - דָּֽבְקָ֣ה at oshb:Ps.119.25 and דָּבַ֥קְתִּי at oshb:Ps.119.31, both byte tier - though calling Ps.119.31 the stanza's closing vow is imprecise when Ps.119.32 is the closing verse. What fails is the cross-seam continuity claim in the rationale, which asserts that the path vocabulary of this stanza is carried over from the close of the preceding stanza. It is not: the preceding stanza carries a path lexeme in 0 of its 8 verses, in either witness. Because the campaign treats a device straddling a row's own seam as an argument for continuity unless disclosed, a false continuity claim is a material evidence defect, and it is the sole prose function of 2 of the 6 entries in boundary_evidence_refs.

challenges.claim: M8-Ps-404's rationale claims DALETH's path vocabulary is carried over from the GIMEL stanza's close, but 0 of the 8 verses Ps.119.17-Ps.119.24 contain any path lexeme in the skeleton or any way/path word in WEB.
challenges.evidence: Skeleton-tier sweep (VERSE counts) over consonantal_index.json for the 4 attested path spellings in this psalm - derek written with final kaf (דרך, spliced from oshb:Ps.119.29), derek written with medial kaf (דרכי, from oshb:Ps.119.26), 'orach (ארחתיך, from oshb:Ps.119.15) and netiv (בנתיב, from oshb:Ps.119.35); final-letter allography is why 2 derek spellings must be swept separately. Union hit counts per stanza: Ps.119.17-Ps.119.24 = 0 verses of 8; Ps.119.25-Ps.119.32 = 5 verses of 8 (Ps.119.26, Ps.119.27, Ps.119.29, Ps.119.30, Ps.119.32); Ps.119.9-Ps.119.16 = 3 verses; Ps.119.1-Ps.119.8 = 3 verses; Ps 119 book-wide = 20 verses. The skeleton of the cited GIMEL close is גם עדתיך שעשעי אנשי עצתי (oshb:Ps.119.24, skeleton tier) - no path lexeme in it. WEB corroborates across the same 8 verses: no way/path word occurs anywhere in Ps.119.17-Ps.119.24, and the closing verse reads “Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors.” (web:Ps.119.24) while the first way-word of the run is at “I declared my ways, and you answered me. Teach me your statutes.” (web:Ps.119.26). The nearest prior path-lexeme verses are Ps.119.14 and Ps.119.15, on the far side of the entire GIMEL stanza, so the vocabulary is not carried across this row's seam at all - it resumes after an 8-verse gap. Repair options are to drop the carry-over clause or to re-anchor it at Ps.119.14-Ps.119.15 with the 8-verse gap disclosed; either way observed_substrate_signals and boundary_evidence_refs (which hold web:Ps.119.17 and web:Ps.119.24 only for this claim) move with it.

reviews.reasoning: Verified independently. הוֹרֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.119.33) and וִֽיבֹאֻ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.119.41) both collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens, the HE letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.33-Ps.119.40, and Ps.119.41 heads a different letter, so the seam at Ps.119.40|Ps.119.41 carries a tier-1 warrant. The form claim needed care because the staged extract has no morphology layer, so I tested it the only way available - pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. WEB renders the verse-initial word as a direct request in 7 of the 8 verses of the span (teach, give understanding, direct, turn, turn, fulfill, take away), and the 8th, web:Ps.119.40, opens on an interjection but still closes with a request, “Behold, I long for your precepts! Revive me in your righteousness.” (web:Ps.119.40) - so the row's statement that the run continues through the stanza's own close is defensible on the evidence available, and the 4 verbs it names in device_notes match the first 4 verses in order. The distinctiveness note is hedged and holds up: the neighbouring DALETH stanza also carries petitions, but not as a verse-initial run, and no other stanza in this cluster shows 7 verse-initial requests. Numbering is identity, citation_sweep.py is GREEN, and pmarks_Ps.json records no selah, paseq or ketiv/qere entry in Ps.119.33-Ps.119.40, so no disclosure is owed. This row's boundary_evidence_refs holds 4 refs and no prose verse sits outside them (check_refs_mirror.py, 0 flags).

Verified independently. וִֽיבֹאֻ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.119.41) and זְכֹר (oshb:Ps.119.49) both collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens - זְכֹר is unaccented in the source, which is expected for this maqaf-free extract and is not a degraded splice, since it matches the first token of oshb:Ps.119.49 exactly. The VAV letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.41-Ps.119.48 and Ps.119.49 heads a different letter. The rejected_alternative is the honest one for this stanza and I checked it rather than accepting it: no selah, no paseq, no ketiv/qere and no reversed-nun or suspended entry falls anywhere in Ps.119.41-Ps.119.48 in pmarks_Ps.json, and a path-lexeme sweep returns 0 verses of 8 here, so there is indeed no interior device competing for a mid-stanza seam. Two observations, neither rising to a challenge. First, describing the stanza's resolve as aimed at scoffers in the plural does not match either witness at the verse it summarizes: WEB reads “So I will have an answer for him who reproaches me, for I trust in your word.” (web:Ps.119.42), a singular reproacher. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the number of the MT token cannot be machine-settled either way - which is itself the reason a plural characterization should not be asserted. Second, the observation that this stanza's letter is also the ordinary conjunction is correct and is properly kept out of the boundary warrant, which rests on the acrostic bytes alone. Confidence high is calibrated.

Verified independently, including the one mark claim in this cluster. זְכֹר (oshb:Ps.119.49) and חֶלְקִ֖י (oshb:Ps.119.57) both collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens; the ZAYIN letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.49-Ps.119.56 and Ps.119.57 heads a different letter. The memory frame is byte-true: a skeleton sweep of the zkr spelling returns 3 verses inside this span - Ps.119.49, Ps.119.52 and Ps.119.55 - and 0 verses in the other seven stanzas of this cluster; the pointed openers זְכֹר (oshb:Ps.119.49) and זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי (oshb:Ps.119.55) are both byte tier, and Ps.119.55 does precede the closing verse Ps.119.56, so the framing statement is accurate. The paseq disclosure checks out against the inventory rather than against received lore: pmarks_Ps.json records paseq in exactly 5 verses of Ps 119 - Ps.119.52, Ps.119.69, Ps.119.104, Ps.119.128 and Ps.119.156 - with a count of 1 at Ps.119.52, which is the verse the row names. Symmetry is complete rather than spot-fixed: Ps.119.52 is the only paseq in the span-relevant set (the span itself plus its two seam verses), so no further disclosure is owed, and 0 of the other 7 rows of this cluster has a paseq in its span. The row labels it single-witness, seg-layer and not quotable as verse bytes, which is the prescribed handling, and denies it boundary force. pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses across all 176 verses of Ps 119, and the row claims none (check_marks.py, 0 flags).

The boundary is sound and I do not contest the span. חֶלְקִ֖י (oshb:Ps.119.57) and ט֭וֹב (oshb:Ps.119.65) collate at byte tier as whole verse-initial tokens, the HETH letter test is exceptionless across the 8 verses Ps.119.57-Ps.119.64, and Ps.119.65 heads a different letter, so the seam at Ps.119.64|Ps.119.65 has a clean tier-1 warrant; numbering is identity, citation_sweep.py is GREEN, check_refs_mirror.py returns 0 flags, and pmarks_Ps.json records no selah, paseq or ketiv/qere entry in this span. The WEB rendering at web:Ps.119.62 is verbatim as summarized. The defect is in device_notes, which builds a two-part characterization of the whole psalm without a sweep behind either part, and both parts fail when swept - one of them against a verse this same cluster cites 7 verses earlier, and the other against this row's own span. Because the campaign requires every claim of this shape to name its object and carry a digit-bearing count, and this one carries none, it is a material evidence defect rather than a wording preference.

The pointed opening of the cited verse is חֲצֽוֹת לַ֗יְלָה (oshb:Ps.119.62, byte tier). Adding the other time-of-day spellings: chatsot 1 verse (Ps.119.62), neshef 1 verse (Ps.119.147), yom 3 verses (Ps.119.91, Ps.119.97, Ps.119.164) - 6 verses of the psalm carry an explicit time marker, not an isolate. On tense: a WEB sweep of Ps 119 returns 35 verses with a past-form rendering and 26 with a future-form rendering, 56 of 176 verses with either; 4 of the 8 verses of this row's own span are among them - “I sought your favor with my whole heart. Be merciful to me according to your word.” (web:Ps.119.58), “I considered my ways, and turned my steps to your statutes.” (web:Ps.119.59), “I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.” (web:Ps.119.60) and web:Ps.119.62 itself, which the note calls a present-tense surround while its own WEB rendering is future. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so a whole-psalm tense claim cannot be machine-verified in either direction; the repair is to drop the characterization or to restate it as a span-scoped observation with the 2-verse layla count disclosed. Ps 119 is identity-numbered, so every ref above needs no dual-cite arithmetic.
